summary: Withdrew three of my own claims: the diamond's forced-equal pair is the degree-2 pair at distance sqrt3 (degree-3 is adjacent, so gluing degree-3 vertices pins nothing); the spindle-minus-closing-edge is NOT induced, the omitted pair being still at unit distance, so the realisation and 'no accidental unit pair' are withdrawn and the abstract two-diamond gluing neither is a translate gluing nor refutes Proposition 2 as stated; and pair-separation does NOT give surjective pair projections or near-rigidity. Recorded the new union result (34 witnesses, all 1048 signatures distinct, no pair pinned), which makes the 1145 survivors obsolete and keeps the union closed. New analysis: an exact criterion for matching certified colouring families across copies under colour permutation - pins form a partial injection sigma on [k], cross edges forbidden cells D in [k]^2, and a bijection extending sigma avoiding D exists. The coupling compresses to a k-by-k object (58 boundary to <=6 pairs, 184 cross to <=36 cells at k=6), independent of the 1048 vertices. Soundness proved (the output re-verifies as a member of J); incompleteness proved and illustrated by a k=3 example where the sampled families fail while the union is a 4-cycle and plainly colourable. Spec given, nothing run.

verified_results.grade: self-withdrawal; PROOF of the corrected degree/force correspondence

verified_results.statement: WITHDRAWAL W2: the Moser spindle minus its closing edge is not an induced unit-distance graph, since the omitted pair remains at unit distance in the embedding, so the induced graph on those 7 points has all 11 edges. 'No accidental unit pair' and the geometric realisation are withdrawn. What survives: the abstract two-diamond gluing is an abstract counterexample only, is not a translate gluing (which identifies p0 with itself), and so does not refute SEED-DESIGN-TAU Proposition 2 in its stated setting. The worker's own R1 remains the accurate account.

WITHDRAWAL W3: pair-separation does not imply that the pair projections are surjective onto [k]^2, nor does it imply near-rigidity. Separation only says that for each pair of vertices some colouring separates them, i.e. the projection's image is not contained in the diagonal. Distinct signatures in a finite family is a statement about that family only.

Recorded (external, not re-derived): the union U of 1048 points now has 34 certified proper 5-colourings with all 1048 vertex signatures distinct and 0 classes of size > 1, so every pair of distinct vertices is separated, no pair is pinned, and the 1145 survivors are obsolete. U remains closed and is not reopened here.

verified_results.statement: Criterion (C) for combining certified families: given phi in Phi_A and psi in Phi_B, the identifications impose forced assignments sigma(psi(v)) = phi(u) and the cross edges impose forbidden cells (psi(y), phi(x)); a valid colour permutation pi of B exists iff sigma is well defined, sigma is injective, and some bijection extends sigma while avoiding D. One permutation applied to B suffices, since (pi_A o phi, pi_B o psi) = (phi, (pi_A^{-1} pi_B) o psi).

Compact representation: the coupling depends on the colourings only through their restrictions to the active set (vertices in I or E_x), so the data reduce to sigma of at most k pairs and D of at most k^2 cells - at k=6, 58 boundary equations become at most 6 pairs and 184 cross edges at most 36 forbidden cells. Nothing depends on the 1048 vertices.

Soundness: if (phi,psi,pi) satisfies the pins and avoids all forbiddens, then (phi, pi o psi) is a member of J - proper on both copies, agreeing on every identification, separating every cross pair. The witness re-verifies from scratch in O(|E_A|+|E_B|+|I|+|E_x|), so it is a certificate, not a solver verdict.

Incompleteness: exhausting Phi_A x Phi_B x S_k without success shows only that J contains no pair built from the sampled families. It does not show J empty and says nothing about k-colourability of the union. Demonstrated by a k=3 example: A and B are 2-edge paths, I identifies both pairs of endpoints, the union is a 4-cycle, the singleton families give inconsistent pins (pi(2)=1 and pi(2)=3) so the method fails, yet the union is plainly colourable; enlarging Phi_A by one colouring makes the combination succeed with an explicit pi.

Implementation specification: validate families (the only step that confers authority), reduce by signature on the active set, per pair build sigma and D and decide by at most k! permutations (720 at k=6) or Hall's condition, emit and re-verify from scratch, then append to the union family and recompute signatures. Cost independent of |V|.

The method is identification-agnostic, so rotated and offset copies are covered unchanged; a rotation only changes which index pairs lie in I and E_x. It does not decide union colourability and does not touch the closed union.

Nothing in this block is evidence of new forcing: no forced pair, no chromatic claim, no plane-level claim. GLUING-CORRECTED.md supersedes the note I audited last block; I have not audited the corrected version and claim nothing about it.

conjectures: For future seeds the binding constraint is likely the pin structure rather than the cross edges: D compresses to at most 36 cells at k=6, so cross edges rarely block a permutation, whereas a single inconsistent pair of pins does. A seed designed so that I contains few vertices with highly correlated colours would be the friendliest to this method.

If the per-copy families are large enough that every signature class on the active set is represented, the combination becomes complete for that active set - a goal worth stating explicitly when a family is grown.

escalation: Precise obstacle for future seeds: the combination method is sound but incomplete, so its failure cannot distinguish 'this seed has no joint colouring from my families' from 'this seed is not colourable'. Closing that gap needs either an UNSAT proof on the union or families large enough to cover every signature class on the active set (at most k^|Act| classes). Expected useful output: families grown until the active-set signature coverage is complete, which would turn the method into a decision procedure for the pinned pairs at least.
